note: Structured, sourced knowledge base for the power-topology design agent (/design-power-topology). Captures the utility-to-chip distribution chain, equipment classes with real ratings + lead times, standard electrical pod blocks, redundancy templates, and Uptime tiers. The deterministic generator (drafts/sld/topology.js) reads this to SIZE a power chain and emit a valid single-line (drafts/sld/engine.js format). `catalogKey` maps a class to data/equipment-catalog.json so the cost model reuses the same pricing/products. Every numeric claim carries a `source`. Primary source for the chain + redundancy is SemiAnalysis 'Datacenter Anatomy Part 1: Electrical Systems'. `architecture_templates.dsx_vr` + the dsx_* equipment classes encode the NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin electrical reference design (source `siemens_dsx`; distilled prose in docs/ai-factory/dsx-vr-architecture.md) — the M2 target topology. Verify exact ratings against the governing NVIDIA RA + project basis of design.

sources.tia942: ANSI/TIA-942 telecommunications infrastructure standard for data centers
sources.siemens_dsx: Siemens UL Reference Design for DSX Vera Rubin NVL72, 100 MW (S&L job DAT-SII-2026-054, 05/2026, 18 sheets) — docs/.reference_archs/Siemens-Schematics-for-DSX-VR.pdf (licensed, gitignored; sheet-by-sheet map in docs/ai-factory/dsx-vr-architecture.md)

voltage_levels.label: High voltage (transmission)
voltage_levels.purpose: Utility transmission into the on-site substation

voltage_levels.label: Medium voltage (site distribution)
voltage_levels.purpose: Campus distribution from the substation to unit-sub transformers; 13.8 kV common in US hyperscale

voltage_levels.label: Low voltage (data hall)
voltage_levels.purpose: UPS output and data-hall delivery; 415 V (line-line) / 240 V (line-neutral) common, 480 V in US

equipment.label: HV substation transformer
equipment.note: Custom-built to the specific transmission interconnect; MVA ≈ MW with a ~5-10% power-factor allowance.

equipment.label: MV switchgear / paralleling
equipment.note: Metal-clad, draw-out breakers, high interrupting rating. Contains breakers, metering, CTs/VTs, switches and MV cables. Paralleling switchgear ties utility ∥ on-site generation; ATS transfers to gensets on outage.

equipment.label: Unit-substation transformer (MV→LV)
equipment.note: One per electrical pod; pairs with the pod UPS. Microsoft pods cited at 3 MVA transformer + 3 MW genset.

equipment.label: Standby generator
equipment.note: Matched to transformer ratings. Diesel preferred (transportable, energy-dense). UPS bridges the ~60 s genset start. Meta 'H' building ~36 gensets; a Google building ~34 larger units.

equipment.label: Static UPS (double-conversion) + battery
equipment.note: Bridges the gap until gensets carry load. Eco/VFD standby mode >99% efficient but adds a few ms transfer time. Losses worsen at low load.

equipment.label: LV main switchboard
equipment.note: Group/fixed-mounted main + feeder breakers — the workhorse LV distribution board. In 2N, deployed as A/B boards.

equipment.label: Overhead busway
equipment.note: Solid copper bars, preferred for high-density. Tap-off units + whips drop to each rack. Replaces per-rack flexible cabling.

equipment.label: Remote power panel (RPP)
equipment.note: Transformer-less row/zone panel fed from a floor PDU or switchboard; branch circuits to a rack cluster via whips. In 2N, deployed as A/B pairs.

equipment.label: OCP power shelf (rack)
equipment.note: Central AC→DC for the whole rack, supplies DC via busbar (Google 48 V). Replaces per-server rectifiers; needs DC-busbar server design.

equipment.label: Battery backup unit (in-rack)
equipment.note: In-rack lithium backup; ride-through at the rack can eliminate dual central UPS systems.

equipment.label: BESS (battery energy storage system)
equipment.note: Ties in at the MV interconnection / point of common coupling (PCC), behind the meter. Buffers between grid-accepted power and internal load; provides fast frequency response, load smoothing, and reactive support — which accelerates grid interconnection (increasingly required by connection codes). A 4-8 h system can also serve the UPS ride-through role (bridge to genset start), i.e. a diesel/UPS alternative.

equipment.label: Utility main transformer (DSX-VR)
equipment.note: One per utility primary; two per site. Sheet E5.0.1 labels read '90/120/150 KVA' — unit typo for MVA (see docs/ai-factory/dsx-vr-architecture.md §6).

equipment.label: 38 kV switchgear lineup (Siemens 8DA10)
equipment.note: SUB1.MSG.A / SUB1.MSG.B: 2500 A main (x-52-1), 16 × 1200 A positions — x-52-2 station aux, x-52-3…15 ring feeders, x-52-16/17 BESS — plus the on-site gen block on a 2500 A x-52-18, a 2500 A tie breaker, and future space. Two lineups per site. Sheet E5.0.1 (B-side BESS tags carry a duplicate-label typo, see doc §6).

equipment.label: 38 kV tie switchgear (SUB1.MSG.T)
equipment.note: Links MSG.A and MSG.B through two normally-open 2500 A breakers (A-52T-1 / B-52T-1); the 15 MVA backup-generation block lands here via 4 × 1200 A gen breakers (4th drawn dashed = future). Sheet E5.0.1.

equipment.label: MV backup-generation block (tie bus)
equipment.note: Sized per E5.0.1 note 1: backup generation ≈ 6% of total IT load + 40% × (6% load) of mechanical load — the core slice only (≈ 0.06 × IT × 1.4 ≈ 8.7 MW at 103 MW IT; 15 MVA drawn = N+1 headroom). Note 2: may be replaced by equivalent on-site base generation.

equipment.label: On-site generation block (optional)
equipment.note: Optional 75 MVA block per 38 kV lineup. Note 3: a mix of resources — thermal units, HRSG, fuel cells, solar. Sheet E5.0.1.

equipment.label: BESS block 37.5 MW / 2 h (DSX-VR)
equipment.note: Note 6: sizing per customer requirements, up to 37.5 MW per 1200 A feeder — enables fully flexible/curtailable load operation and supports grid-interconnection acceleration. Connects at dedicated MV feeders, never behind a DU transformer. Sheet E5.0.1.

equipment.label: RMU skid — 34.5 kV 4-way switch (600 A)
equipment.note: Skid-mounted ring main unit: two ring ways + local transformer tee-offs. Six per deployment unit (RMU1–6), plus 6 core-load skids per site. Sheets E5.0.1/E5.0.2 skid boxes; views 1–6.

equipment.label: Compute MVT 4.2 MVA, 34.5 kV→480 V (VPI)
equipment.note: One per MSB-GPU; four per DU (RMU1–4). Grid-direct compute — no UPS downstream. Views 1–4.

equipment.label: Support MVT 2.0 MVA, 34.5 kV→415/240 V (VPI)
equipment.note: Two per DU, on the RMU1 and RMU3 skids; feeds MSB-SUPP. Views 1 & 3.

equipment.label: Chiller MVT 4.2 MVA, 34.5 kV→2.4/4.16 kV (VPI)
equipment.note: Two per DU (RMU5, RMU6); feeds MSB-CHILLERS (MV chillers). View 5.

equipment.label: Mech MVT 1.5 MVA, 34.5 kV→480 V (VPI)
equipment.note: Two per DU (RMU5, RMU6); feeds MSB-MECH. CONTRADICTION IN SOURCE: campus sheets label the secondary 415 V, Views 5–6 and the MSB-MECH board rating say 480 V; 480 V adopted — confirm per doc §6. Core variant MVT-6 is 34.5 kV → 277/480 V 3Ph-4W. View 5; MSB-MECH1 sheet.

equipment.label: Core-IT MVT 4.2 MVA, 34.5 kV→415 V (MVT-1…4)
equipment.note: One per MSB-SUPP1…4 (core 'NETWORK/CONTROL/SHARE'). CONTRADICTION IN SOURCE: letter sheets also carry a 'MVT-1 / 415V / 3 MVA' callout beside the 4.2 MVA symbol; 4.2 adopted (2-of-3 labels, matches the 5000 A board) — confirm per doc §6. MSB-SUPP1 sheet.

equipment.label: Core chiller MVT-5, 3 MVA, 34.5 kV→2.4/4.16 kV
equipment.note: Feeds the core MSB-CHILLER boards (dual interlocked 600 A incomers with GS-5/GS-7). MSB-CHILLERS 1&2 sheet.

equipment.label: MSB-GPU — 5000 A, 480 V, 3Ph-3W
equipment.note: Compute switchboard; four per DU, one per 4.2 MVA compute MVT. Grid-direct (no UPS). View 1 (sheet main reads '5000AT/5000AT' — frame/trip typo normalized, doc §6).

equipment.label: MSB-SUPP (DU) — 3000 A, 415/240 V, 3Ph-4W
equipment.note: DU support-load board; two per DU (RMU1/RMU3 skids). View 1 & 3.

equipment.label: MSB-CHILLERS — 1200 A, 2.4/4.16 kV, 3Ph-4W
equipment.note: MV chiller board; two per DU (chillers 1–4 / 5–8). Core variant: dual interlocked 600 A '52' incomers (MVT-5 / GS-5·GS-7). View 5; MSB-CHILLERS 1&2 sheet.

equipment.label: MSB-MECH — 2000 A, 480 V, 3Ph-3W
equipment.note: DU mechanical board; two per DU. Core variant MSB-MECH1/2: 277/480 V 3Ph-4W, dual interlocked 2000AF/2000AT LSIG incomers (MVT-6 / GS-6·GS-8), feeders 1200AF/800AT LSIG. View 5; MSB-MECH1 sheet.

equipment.label: MSB-SUPP1…4 (core IT) — 5000 A, 415 V, 3Ph-4W
equipment.incomers: dual interlocked 5000AF/5000AT LSIG (MVT / generator) + 5000AF/5000AT bus sections
equipment.feeders: 4 × 600AF/400AT LSI → RPP 400 A · 2 × 2000AF/2000AT LSIG → busway 2000 A · 4 × 3000AF/2500AT LSIG (dedicated input + output breaker per UPS) · 150AF/125AT gen aux · 5000AF/5000AT load bank
equipment.note: Core 'NETWORK/CONTROL/SHARE' board — the only UPS-backed boards in the design (2 × 1.5 MVA per board). Four per site. MSB-SUPP1 sheet.

equipment.label: RPP 1000 A (compute rows)
equipment.note: Eight per MSB-GPU (32 per DU). View 1.

equipment.label: RPP 800 A (support)
equipment.note: Four per MSB-SUPP (8 per DU). View 1.

equipment.label: RPP 400 A (core IT)
equipment.note: Four per MSB-SUPP1…4 (16 per site). MSB-SUPP1 sheet.

equipment.label: Core UPS 1.5 MVA (double-conversion, Li-ion)
equipment.note: Two per core-IT board (8 per site) — the ONLY UPS in the DSX-VR design; compute is grid-direct. MSB-SUPP1 sheet.

equipment.label: Core-IT generator GS-1…4 — 2.8 MW/3.5 MVA, 415/240 V (opt.)
equipment.note: Optional (note 4: backup generation at LV level for core load); interlocked second incomer of MSB-SUPP1…4 via 5000AF/5000AT LSIG-100%; load-bank camlock connectors + generator enclosure panel. MSB-SUPP1 sheet (campus label reads '2.8 MVA (OPT.)' — letter-sheet MW/MVA values adopted, doc §6).

equipment.label: Core chiller generator GS-5/GS-7 — 2.8 MW/3.5 MVA, 2.4/4.16 kV (opt.)
equipment.note: Optional; interlocked second incomer of the core MSB-CHILLER boards via 600AF/600AT LSIG-100%; load-bank camlocks. MSB-CHILLERS 1&2 / 3&4 sheets.

equipment.label: Core mech generator GS-6/GS-8 — 1.5 MW/1.875 MVA, 277/480 V (opt.)
equipment.note: Optional; interlocked second incomer of MSB-MECH1/2 via 2000AF/2000AT LSIG-100%; load-bank camlocks. MSB-MECH1/2 sheets.

equipment.label: Core busway 2000 A, 415/240 V, 3Ph-4W
equipment.note: Two per core-IT board, on 2000AF/2000AT LSIG feeders. MSB-SUPP1 sheet.

substation_topologies.label: Main-Tie-Main (secondary-selective / double-ended)
substation_topologies.tie: one tie breaker, normally-open (interlocked) or normally-closed for critical DC loads
substation_topologies.note: Two equal-kVA HV/MV transformers feed two MV buses (A/B) with two main breakers (N.C.) and a tie breaker. Loss of one source transfers load to the other bus; allows maintenance on one transformer with no outage. The Drybulb default MV arrangement.

substation_topologies.label: Ring Main Unit (RMU) loop
substation_topologies.note: Closed-loop MV feed; each RMU has two incoming feeders → redundant paths. Isolates a faulted section while maintaining service. Common where the local utility provides a looped MV feed; the RMU is the switching node between incoming utility feeders and outgoing transformer feeders.

substation_topologies.label: Distributed redundant (3-to-2 / 4-to-3, catcher)
substation_topologies.note: M blocks share a bus, any M−1 carry the load (each ~67-75% loaded). A 'catcher' variant keeps one reserve block online-unloaded that catches a failed block via Static Transfer Switch (STS). Applied at the UPS layer (see redundancy_templates). Beyond 4-to-make-3 = diminishing returns.

substation_topologies.label: System-plus-system (2N)
substation_topologies.note: Two fully independent A/B systems end-to-end. Highest availability (Tier IV), highest CapEx. Applied at the UPS + distribution layers (see redundancy_templates).

substation_topologies.label: DSX-VR dual-lineup + dual-ended 34.5 kV loops
substation_topologies.tie: separate tie switchgear (SUB1.MSG.T), two normally-open 2500 A breakers, backup-gen block on the tie bus
substation_topologies.note: Two independent 38 kV lineups (each from its own utility primary) distribute through dual-ended open-loop rings at 34.5 kV: each ring leaves an A-lineup 1200 A feeder, daisy-chains one RMU position across four deployment units, and lands on a B-lineup feeder. Normal state is radial (one open point per ring); the second end is the maintenance/failure path. Concurrent maintainability lives at MV — no 2N duplication of the LV plant, and compute is grid-direct (UPS/generators exist only on the core block).

generator_voltage.label: Low-voltage gensets (≈480 V)
generator_voltage.note: 400/480 V gensets land on a TRANSFER switchboard (SWBD-A/B) upstream of each side's UPS, switching that UPS's source between normal (the unit-sub transformer(s), aggregated through a Normal bus when there's more than one per side) and emergency (the generator) — never both live. This is the Drybulb default; feeding the MV bus instead requires step-up. [assumption] the transfer arrangement itself is Drybulb's modeling choice, corrected 2026-09 from an earlier paralleling-switchboard draft (`gensource` describes hyperscale generator PARALLELING switchgear generally, not this specific transfer topology — cited for genset class/rating context, not as the source for the transfer-vs-parallel choice).

generator_voltage.label: Medium-voltage gensets (3.3-13.8 kV)
generator_voltage.note: Direct MV gensets feed the MV bus without step-up transformers; chosen on large (>10-20 MW) campuses to cut cable/transformer-yard cost.

pod_blocks_mw.note: Standardised pod size — widely available equipment, lower cost
Standardised pod size; common transformer/UPS granularity

redundancy_templates.label: Distributed redundant (4-to-make-3)
redundancy_templates.meaning: M blocks share a bus, any M−1 carry load; each UPS ~75% loaded

redundancy_templates.label: Distributed redundant (3-to-make-2)
redundancy_templates.meaning: 3 blocks per 2 needed share a bus

redundancy_templates.label: Catcher / N+2C (isolated parallel)
redundancy_templates.meaning: a reserve UPS 'catches' a failed block via Static Transfer Switch (STS) — ~2N availability, lower cost

dsx_vr.label: NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin — 100 MW reference design (Siemens UL)

backup_generation.sizing_note_verbatim: BACKUP GENERATION ≈ 6% OF TOTAL IT LOAD + 40% × (6% LOAD) OF MECHANICAL LOAD.
backup_generation.substitution: may be replaced by equivalent on-site base generation (note 2)

deployment_unit.identical_note: DU1–DU4 electrically identical to DU5–DU8 excluding core IT (note 5)

core.purpose: 'NETWORK/CONTROL/SHARE' (E5.0.1) — the only UPS- and generator-backed load

invariants: Compute path = utility → 38 kV lineup → 34.5 kV ring → RMU → 4.2 MVA MVT → MSB-GPU → RPP 1000 A → rack; no UPS/genset/ATS on this path
Every ring is dual-ended (A-feeder + B-feeder) with a normal open point
UPS only downstream of core-IT 415 V boards; generators only as interlocked second incomers of core boards or the 15 MVA backup block on the tie
Voltage discipline: 38 kV bus / 34.5 kV rings; 480 V 3Ph-3W compute + DU mech; 415/240 V 3Ph-4W support + core IT; 2.4/4.16 kV chillers; 277/480 V core mech
DU quantization: whole DUs only (fixed skid/board/RPP kit); exactly one core block per site
BESS on dedicated MV feeders ≤ 37.5 MW each, never behind a DU transformer; on-site generation at MV; backup block on the tie
Schedule and graph derive from one spec: per-DU kit × DU count + core + site gear
